# `test/fixtures/config/` — M6 (#8) config-text fixtures

**Hand-authored. Not captured from a device.** cEOS-lab is not installed on the machine M6 was written
on, and the offline suite never talks to the 7050TX-64, so these `.conf` files were written from
documented EOS 4.28 config forms by hand. `docs/TESTING.md` §4 asks for hand-authored config text to be
marked; the marker lives here and in `manifest.json` rather than inside the `.conf` files, because EOS
config text has no comment syntax — a `# SYNTHETIC …` line would itself be parsed as a section
(`chunkConfig` would answer with a key named `'# SYNTHETIC …'`), which is the opposite of a fixture
that shows what the parser does.

| File | What it pins |
|---|---|
| `acl-sections.conf` | `ip access-list standard …` and `ip access-list …` (extended) blocks: `host`/`prefix`/wildcard/`any` rules, operators (`eq 161`, `neq snmp`, `lt 1024`), trailing option tokens, a `no statistics per-entry` line and a body-less ACL (W2b #37) |
| `banner-eof.conf` | EOF-terminated `banner login` / `banner motd` at indent 0, blank line inside the body |
| `banner-indented-not-multiline.conf` | the **limitation**: the banner rule is indent-0 only, so an indented `banner` is not a multiline block and its `EOF` becomes a sibling key |
| `code-unit-control-functions.conf` | `code unit` continuation lines, and the swallowed-rest-of-config consequence of an **indented** `EOF` |
| `mac-security-profile.conf` | nested `profile` sub-sections, including a profile with no body |
| `minimal-with-blank-line.conf` | blank line → the `''` section key; repeated `!` markers collapsing into one `'!'` key |
| `qos-class-policy-map.conf` | `class-map` / `policy-map` with `class` sub-blocks; the wrong-level match trap |
| `router-bgp-address-family.conf` | three nesting levels (`router bgp` → `vrf` → `address-family`) and sub-section-before-parent key order |
| `switchport-trunk.conf` | `switchport trunk allowed vlan 10-12,20,30-33`, `native vlan`, access mode, quoted `description`, `port-channel … member interface` |
| `unhandled-literal-blank-line.conf` | **negative**: `ConfigParseError`, blank line + under-length `   !` |
| `unhandled-literal-short-line.conf` | **negative**: `ConfigParseError`, `   !` shorter than the body indent |
| `varp-virtual-router.conf` | the global `ip virtual-router mac-address` line, `ip virtual-router address …` on VLAN interfaces (one, two, none), and a routed `interface Ethernet1` VARP line that upstream's `^interface (Vlan\d+)$` scan — and this client — do not read (W2b #37) |
| `vlan-blocks.conf` | `vlan 1`, `vlan 10 / name`, ranged `vlan 11-13` header, quoted `name`, `state suspend`, two `trunk group` lines |

## `pyeapi-oracle.json`

Ordered `[key, value]` entries produced by **upstream pyeapi** running `_chunkify` over each fixture,
generated by `../../scripts/config-chunkify-oracle.py` (pyeapi 1.0.4-rc0, `develop` `6816d9e`, CPython
3.13). It is the parity target for `src/config/chunk.fixture.test.ts`: the TypeScript chunker must
produce the same keys, in the same order, with the same values — and the same error text shape for the
two negative fixtures. It records what **pyeapi** does with these bytes; it is not evidence about EOS,
and it must be regenerated (not hand-edited) if upstream changes:

```
python3 arista-api-client/scripts/config-chunkify-oracle.py         # rewrite
python3 arista-api-client/scripts/config-chunkify-oracle.py --check  # report drift
```
